sources_considered.why: Read to identify Mollick's linked paper; not used to establish the study's findings.
Original study version available before Marcus's post.
The study authors explicitly explain its performance and capability findings.

receipt.public_excerpt: We want to estimate the rate at which newer language models are able to achieve a certain level of performance more efficiently than older models.

evidence_items.explanation: The study measures efficiency at a given performance level. Its compute-halving estimate does not establish that capabilities themselves doubled at the same rate.

receipt.public_excerpt: Nevertheless, our work provides a rigorous quantitative analysis of the remarkable rate of progress in language modeling capabilities over the past decade.

evidence_items.explanation: The authors explicitly describe an analysis of improving capabilities. Their summary also explains the study's decomposition of performance gains into compute scaling and algorithmic contributions, contradicting the assertion that it addresses only efficiency.
